name: CHIPS Program Office awards and proposed funding registry
known_limitations: The registry mixes direct funding awards with proposed funding announcements. A named place, proposed amount, or signed award does not establish disbursement, construction completion, commissioning, accepted output, utilization, employment realized, or project outcome; each entry must retain its own legal and milestone state.
source_owner: National Institute of Standards and Technology
automation_notes: Preserve the exact award-versus-proposal state, named facility, amount boundary, artifact date, and excluded inference for every place-system use.
factual_nucleus: The registry identifies direct awards including up to $18 million for Edwards Vacuum in Genesee County, $1.45 billion for GlobalFoundries in Malta, $125 million for GlobalFoundries in Burlington, and up to $32 million for Corning in Canton; it separately labels Sumika in Baytown and Analog Devices in Beaverton and Camas as proposed funding.
notes: Phase 178 named-place registry anchor checked 2026-09-01. Inclusion does not establish a project stage or outcome. The current registry identifies named activity in places including Genesee County, Malta, Burlington, Canton, Baytown, Easton, Beaverton, and Camas while retaining entry-specific funding status.
